title: What If You Held Your Breath as Long as You Could?

scenes.text: What if you held your breath as long as you could? The burning isn't what you think.
Most people last 30 seconds to two minutes. The urge isn't lack of oxygen. It's carbon dioxide building up.
By two or three minutes, your diaphragm spasms as it tries to force a breath.
Around three to five minutes, you'd get lightheaded as less oxygenated blood reaches your brain.
Past about six minutes you'd black out, and automatic breathing takes over. That's why nobody should try this in water.
The Guinness record is 29 minutes 3 seconds by a Croatian freediver, after nine months of training and a last breath from an oxygen tank.
